findings.reviewerJudgement: ACCEPTED as consistent with D10 as written. I note the tension the receipt does not: D10's clause 'afterwards ... enters `blocked`' describes the state a campaign reaches when the window has CLOSED, which reads against rolling back out of it. But a campaign blocked by a parity MISMATCH (the other route into `blocked`) has by construction committed nothing of its own, so both guards genuinely pass — and because src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAuthorityMode.ts:105-112 maps marker state 'blocked' to authority kind 'blocked' (which campaignAcceptsCommands at :119-121 refuses outright), rollback is that campaign's ONLY exit. reasoning: The decision logic is ALREADY under src/ and IS typechecked. Every gate, every state transition and every typed refusal lives in src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignAuthorityCutoverOps.ts, which the root project compiles — `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` exited 0 in this session. scripts/campaign-authority-cutover.ts is already the thin wrapper the question proposes: its whole body is parse (:81-93), init (:112-113), dispatch (:116-119), print + exit-code map (:121-125). The stack's own precedent already accepts tracked-but-untypechecked top-level CLIs: .gitignore:41-42 allowlists scripts/print-combat-validation-gaps.ts and scripts/expand-unit-type-requirements.mjs, and scripts/cleanup-broken-encounters.ts (the shape this file copied, including its test location) sits in exactly the same position. Adding a third is uniform with the stack, not a new exception.

I EXECUTED the CLI this session, which the receipt could not claim: `npx tsx scripts/campaign-authority-cutover.ts --help` printed the usage and exited 0; `npx tsx scripts/campaign-authority-cutover.ts parrity x` printed `error: Unknown command: parrity` plus the usage and exited 1. No database is opened on either path (resetSQLiteService is at :112, after parsing).

Moving the entry point under src/ would pull an operator maintenance CLI into the Next.js build graph for a file with zero decisions in it — a larger and less uniform change than the residual risk warrants.

findings.title: A marker-io exception now turns a COMMITTED command into an error response
findings.detail: recordFirstCommandOnMarker (src/lib/campaign/authority/campaignCommandPipeline.ts:344-353) calls durableCampaignMarkerIo.read and .write with no try/catch, as the first statement of acknowledgeCommit (:355) — i.e. AFTER the batch has committed. A throw from either propagates out of acknowledgeCommit, out of executeCampaignCommand (which has no catch), into the route's try/catch at src/pages/api/campaigns/[id]/commands.ts:129 and out through sendCaughtApiError. The client would be told its command FAILED when the journal has already committed it. Before this change that path could not throw.
whyNotBlocking: Unreachable today: CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED is false (src/lib/campaign/sync/JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:84), so no campaign reaches journal authority.
Self-recovering: a client retry with the same commandId hits command-identity-conflict and returns {kind:'duplicate'} -> HTTP 200 (campaignCommandPipeline.ts:543-545; commands.ts:158-164).
Fail-safe for D10 even if the marker never gets stamped — proven by mutant M1 in this session (rollback stays prohibited via journal-head-past-baseline).

The realistic trigger is a genuine SQLite fault that would have broken the append first; the benign cases are already handled (uninitialized service -> null at campaignCutoverMarkerIo.ts:42; corrupt row -> null at :44).
findings.recommendation: At the slice that flips the flag, decide between (a) wrapping the marker report in try/catch + a logged warning — honest, since the fail-safe is proven, but it does swallow a real DB fault; or (b) making the stamp ATOMIC with the append. Option (b) is precedented in this codebase and is the stronger fix: src/lib/events/journal/SQLiteEventJournalWriter.ts:56 documents appendWithExtension as existing precisely so 'durable consumers make a receipt ... inside the same SQLite transaction', and src/lib/campaign/sync/campaignCombatOutcomeInbox.ts:80 already uses `journal.appendWithExtension(batch, (db, append) => {...})` for exactly this. It would mean appendCampaignCommandBatch accepting an extension, which touches 5 call sites — correctly out of scope for a composition-only slice, which is why this is a recommendation and not a required edit. The receipt's openQuestion 2 raises the atomicity question but does not name the available mechanism; it should.
